packs.title: Active Directory and Windows Identity Security
packs.entry: Demonstrate Windows users/groups, basic DNS and TCP/IP, and permission inspection.
packs.limits: Real Windows domain, GPO and AD CS exercises require isolated licensed/evaluation Windows VMs or a hosted lab. GOAD orchestrates Windows VMs; its Docker launcher does not make domain controllers Pi containers.
packs.verification: 18 server-graded concept/micro-exercise checks; 16 hands-on artifact checks requiring evidence review.

packs.title: AI and LLM Application Security
packs.entry: Understand HTTP, JSON, application authorization and the difference between model output and trusted program state.
packs.limits: Use deterministic mock models and synthetic data first. These tests validate application boundaries, not the general resistance of a real language model; real-model testing needs a separately configured model and budget.
packs.verification: 18 server-graded concept/micro-exercise checks; 16 hands-on artifact checks requiring evidence review.

packs.title: API Security and Authorization Engineering
packs.entry: Read HTTP and JSON, use two synthetic accounts and explain authentication versus authorization.
packs.limits: Use designated lessons and owned API fixtures. GraphQL introspection or a visible route alone is not a vulnerability.
packs.verification: 18 server-graded concept/micro-exercise checks; 16 hands-on artifact checks requiring evidence review.

packs.title: Cloud Security: Identity, Exposure and Detection
packs.entry: Explain HTTP, role-based access and basic JSON; distinguish cloud control-plane actions from workload traffic.
packs.limits: Local policy fixtures teach reasoning; actual AWS/Azure/GCP enforcement requires a scoped training account. CloudGoat creates real billable resources and is not provisioned automatically.
packs.verification: 18 server-graded concept/micro-exercise checks; 16 hands-on artifact checks requiring evidence review.

packs.title: Container and Kubernetes Security
packs.entry: Run a local container, identify its image and mounts, and explain processes and file permissions.
packs.limits: Docker exercises work on the supported Pi profiles. Kubernetes enforcement needs a real disposable cluster and a CNI that implements NetworkPolicy; YAML validation alone is not runtime evidence.
packs.verification: 18 server-graded concept/micro-exercise checks; 16 hands-on artifact checks requiring evidence review.

packs.title: Applied Cryptography and Protocol Security
packs.entry: Work with bytes, hexadecimal and small Python programs; distinguish encoding from encryption.
packs.limits: Use established libraries and training data. Toy arithmetic explains mechanisms; it is not production cryptographic implementation guidance.
packs.verification: 18 server-graded concept/micro-exercise checks; 16 hands-on artifact checks requiring evidence review.

packs.title: Defensive Security & Detection
packs.entry: Use the entry demonstration in the track to check your background.
packs.limits: Established v3 assessment rubric; file checks do not grade reasoning.
packs.verification: See each task: automated evidence, artifact checks and human assessment have different scope.

packs.title: DevOps 2: Delivery & Infrastructure Automation
packs.description: Test every change, promote the same artifact, and recreate owned infrastructure with explicit trust and cleanup.
packs.entry: Enter after you can run, inspect and recover a small service; prior equivalent practice is valid.
background: Git/file/terminal basics, service/version/state distinctions, and owned Docker or Linux guests for operational tasks.
packs.limits: Local rehearsal works without a paid account. Real CI needs a learner-owned repository; Terraform/OpenTofu and Ansible act only on the chosen learner environment. No shared server execution or automatic cloud spending.
packs.verification: Manual operational review; runnable local controls for service, state, release and failure/recovery. Local reports are not automatic verified skill results.

packs.title: DevOps 3: Reliability, Recovery & Orchestration
packs.description: Measure useful service behaviour, control overload, restore data, and operate a small Kubernetes deployment.
packs.entry: Enter when you can deploy and trace a versioned service and have used an owned Linux/container environment.
background: Service/network/state basics; delivery practices from track 2 or equivalent prior work. Kubernetes uses a separate local-cluster budget.
packs.limits: Most checks run locally. A VM/cluster, real monitoring binary and optional CI account are needed for their corresponding operational outcomes. Same-PC replicas do not prove physical high availability.
packs.verification: Manual operational review; runnable local controls for service, state, release and failure/recovery. Local reports are not automatic verified skill results.

packs.title: DevOps 1: Service & Deployment Foundations
packs.description: Take Relay from a local process to a versioned service, private edge, guest deployment and container.
packs.entry: Start here if processes, HTTP, Linux service operation or deployment boundaries are new.
background: Basic file/editor use. A guided Linux guest setup is available through the Infrastructure VM track; Python, shell and networking are explained as used.
packs.limits: Local tools and owned Linux guests. No cloud subscription required. Public exposure and physical hardware are optional later variants; manual operational completion is not an automatic verified skill result.
packs.verification: Manual operational review; runnable local controls for service, state, release and failure/recovery. Local reports are not automatic verified skill results.

packs.title: Digital Forensics and Incident Response
packs.entry: Handle files, compute hashes and interpret timestamps without modifying the original evidence.
packs.limits: Use licensed public datasets and synthetic artifacts. Large disk/memory images may exceed Pi storage; Windows memory interpretation needs symbols/tools matching the supplied image.
packs.verification: 18 server-graded concept/micro-exercise checks; 16 hands-on artifact checks requiring evidence review.

packs.title: Ethical Hacking Foundations
packs.entry: Use a terminal, explain an IP address and HTTP request, and create a disposable local target.
packs.limits: An entry pathway into web, network and directory testing; not certification equivalence or permission to test third parties.
packs.verification: 18 server-graded concept/micro-exercise checks; 16 hands-on artifact checks requiring evidence review.

packs.title: Malware Analysis with Safe Training Artifacts
packs.entry: Read simple code and binary metadata, understand hashes and distinguish static from dynamic analysis.
packs.limits: Start with benign toy programs and published traces. Live malware must not run in these Docker labs; it requires an appropriately isolated VM environment and reviewed sample handling. REMnux now offers ARM64 appliances, but individual tools and Pi deployment remain separate compatibility questions.
packs.verification: 18 server-graded concept/micro-exercise checks; 16 hands-on artifact checks requiring evidence review.

packs.title: Mobile Application Security
packs.entry: Understand HTTP and application permissions; use an owned test device or appropriate emulator.
packs.limits: MASTG practice apps and an Android/iOS test environment are required for operational assessments. A Pi Docker container is not an Android/iOS emulator; fixtures are preparation, not a substitute for device evidence.
packs.verification: 18 server-graded concept/micro-exercise checks; 16 hands-on artifact checks requiring evidence review.

packs.entry: Read network diagrams and distinguish operational safety from information confidentiality.
packs.limits: Use software simulators and supplied captures only. No real PLC, safety system or industrial network is targeted; a simulator cannot establish physical safety.
packs.verification: 18 server-graded concept/micro-exercise checks; 16 hands-on artifact checks requiring evidence review.

packs.title: Red Teaming and Adversary Emulation
packs.entry: Demonstrate scoped enumeration, identity/permission reasoning and the ability to inspect defender telemetry.
packs.limits: Assumed-breach, controlled emulation with harmless markers. Windows enterprise exercises need an isolated VM lab; no covert implants, live credential theft or production phishing are provisioned.

packs.title: Security Architecture, Risk and Governance
packs.entry: Understand service users, data and business purpose; distinguish a requirement from evidence.
packs.limits: Uses public NIST guidance and fictional organizations. Completion is not an audit attestation or legal/compliance advice.

packs.title: SOC Analyst: Triage, Investigation and Response

packs.title: Threat Hunting and Threat Intelligence

packs.limits: Use public reports and synthetic telemetry; this track does not authorize investigating private individuals or scanning report indicators.

packs.title: Verified security lab: solve and show the result
